content.text:
The crash came from `powerline-zsh.py` using `sys.getdefaultencoding()`, which is `'ascii'` on Python 2. Your branch `fix🦠` is UTF-8 from git, so decoding it as ASCII failed on the emoji byte (`0xf0`).

I changed the encoding to `'utf-8'`, which is what git uses for ref names:

```13:13:/Users/sinchunyeung/dev/powerline-zsh/powerline-zsh.py
encoding = 'utf-8'
```

The script runs cleanly now and shows `fix🦠` in the prompt. Open a new terminal tab (or re-source your zsh config) if your prompt still looks stale.
